title: Independent counter-review of T30-R1 and proposed test seam

source_binding.method: SHA-256 recomputed over target-commit raw files previously downloaded from immutable raw URLs; hashes match the independent T33 source binding.

request_path.evidence: dbinder_base_invoker_process.h: TargetStubSendRequest holds this invoker's objectMutex_, obtains auto* stub = current->QueryStubByIndex(cookie), checks null, then invokes IPCObjectStub::SendRequest through the raw pointer. No sptr construction or IncStrongRef occurs between lookup and call. The lock remains held through SendRequest.
request_path.counter_review: The per-invoker lock is not by itself a lifetime pin. It only blocks teardown paths using the same mutex instance.

close_path.evidence: databus_socket_listener.cpp: ServerOnShutdown obtains the DBinder invoker from the callback thread's IPCThreadSkeleton and calls OnDatabusSessionServerSideClosed. dbinder_databus_invoker.cpp: that method detaches the socket/session and app-auth rows, locks GetObjectMutex(), looks up each remaining stub index and calls DecStrongRef(this).
close_path.counter_review: No source-level guarantee found that callback and request worker share a TLS skeleton/invoker. If they are distinct threads, their non-static objectMutex_ fields are distinct, so this lock does not serialize the two paths. Same-thread execution would serialize, but target SoftBus dispatch/thread evidence is unavailable.

index_and_destruction.evidence: ipc_process_skeleton.cpp: QueryStubByIndex uses stubObjectsMutex_ while finding the raw map entry and returns the pointer after releasing the shared lock; EraseStubIndex takes the unique map lock. ipc_object_stub.cpp: OnLastStrongRef erases the index and detaches auth state.
index_and_destruction.counter_review: Erase prevents a later lookup from finding the entry but cannot invalidate an already copied raw pointer. If close completes before lookup, lookup returns null (fail-closed). If lookup returns first, this map lock does not keep the object alive.

reference_count.evidence: Session relation establishment increments a strong reference; close detaches each socket relation and performs one DecStrongRef per returned relation. OnLastStrongRef handles final release.
reference_count.counter_review: The socket relation can mechanically be the final ref, but source alone does not establish reference distribution for a real target stub at an overlap point. Other sptr owners would keep it alive.

existing_test_coverage.basis: Pinned-target test inventory from T30 and T32 reports; no test execution performed in this task.
coverage_found: IPCObjectStub DBinder INCREFS/DECREFS handler unit cases exercise handler branches, not a synchronized request-versus-close interleaving.
DBinderDatabusInvoker OnDatabusSessionServerSideClosed unit/fuzz cases exercise close handling in isolation.
IPCProcessSkeleton attach/detach fuzz routines exercise relation operations without a concurrent transaction gate.
existing_test_coverage.gap: No identified target test pauses after successful raw QueryStubByIndex and coordinates a distinct callback thread to detach the same socket relation before SendRequest.

runtime_and_pairing.product_build_execution: not available in reviewed evidence; T32 records no matching OHOS clang/sysroot or generated target build files and no manifest pairing the target IPC commit with SoftBus
runtime_and_pairing.interpretation: These gaps prevent confirmation; they do not refute the source-level raw-pointer window.

verdict.candidate: T30-R1 remains one low-confidence conditional raw-pointer lifetime candidate: a distinct-thread close callback could detach the socket's last strong reference after lookup and before/during SendRequest. No static strong-ref pin, shared cross-thread mutex, or index-erasure mechanism was found that closes that exact interleaving.
verdict.strongest_refuting_edge: Close-before-lookup: close releases the relation and last-ref teardown erases the index; a later QueryStubByIndex returns null and SendRequest is skipped. Also, an unrelated remaining strong owner or a callback on the same serialized thread prevents this particular destruction schedule.
do_not_promote_without: proof the socket relation is the last strong ref
target runtime observation of destruction before a subsequent SendRequest access and concrete impact

minimum_test_oracle.seam: Test-only barrier immediately after QueryStubByIndex returns non-null and before SendRequest; do not pause while holding a map lock (the lookup has already released it).
red_schedule: Create a target stub whose same socket relation is demonstrably its only strong ref.
On request worker, pass caller gate, obtain raw pointer and pause at the seam.
On a distinct thread-local IPC invoker, close that socket and wait for DecStrongRef-to-zero, OnLastStrongRef/destruction marker, and index erase.
Release the request worker and instrument whether SendRequest entry/access occurs after the destruction marker; run under the target product sanitizer/instrumented build.
minimum_test_oracle.green_oracle: With a test-only strong sptr pin acquired before the raw pointer can outlive lookup and held through SendRequest, the destructor must not run before the call exits; releasing the pin then permits exactly one final destruction. This is an oracle design only, not a proposed production patch.
controls: close-before-lookup returns null and skips SendRequest
an unrelated strong owner keeps the object alive through the call
request finishes before close and close releases the relation once
minimum_test_oracle.safety_limit: Do not deliberately perform an uncontrolled dangling dereference. A red result requires a controlled target test showing destructor-before-call and instrumented post-destruction access (or sanitizer evidence), not merely refcount zero/index erase.

summary: Independent review does not find a source-level refutation of the lookup-before-close window. Candidate stays conditional (0 confirmed, 1 conditional). Dynamic thread overlap, last-ref state, post-destruction access, and impact remain unproven; existing reported unit/fuzz coverage does not test the interleaving.
